recent_notebooks.summary: Evidence suggests that users have a persistent, stable preference for 'flow' states—defined as a balance between task difficulty and skill. AI systems aiming to support this preference must avoid disrupting this state with static or intrusive interventions.
recent_notebooks.title: Flow-State as an Emergent Preference

review.alternative: Implicitly distributed reasoning in monolithic prompts may offer better latent performance at the cost of interpretability.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that monolithic models consistently outperform decoupled agents on justification tasks without auxiliary memory.

claims.statement: Architectural separation of cognition, control, and memory can make the justificatory basis of AI decisions explicit.

support.explanation: This separation allows the system to treat the 'control' (governing axioms) as a discrete, inspectable entity rather than an opaque part of the cognition prompt.
support.passage: The Structured Cognitive Loop (SCL) is introduced as an architectural alternative that separates these functions. In SCL, the language model is dedicated to cognition only, execution is governed by a lightweight controller that mediates every proposal before any action is taken, and memory is maintained externally as a structured store of verified facts.

review.alternative: Self-correction limitations are due to insufficient scale rather than fundamental methodology.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of smaller models achieving robust self-correction without external teacher-model supervision.

claims.statement: Teacher-guided supervision overcomes the inherent limitations of solo self-correction in smaller models.

support.explanation: SuperCorrect demonstrates that 'correcting' a model's logic requires an external validation process, supporting the idea that models struggle with identifying their own foundational reasoning errors independently.
support.passage: To overcome these limitations, we propose SuperCorrect, a novel two-stage framework that uses a large teacher model to supervise and correct both the reasoning and reflection processes of a smaller student model.

actions.findings:
Architectural separation of cognition, control, and memory can make the justificatory basis of AI decisions explicit. [source-51196608d740480b]

Teacher-guided supervision overcomes the inherent limitations of solo self-correction in smaller models. [source-90a697b24b434444]
actions.limitations: Current methods like SCL and SuperCorrect externalize control or supervision, meaning the 'identification' of axioms is still largely engineered by the designer rather than autonomously generated by the model.
actions.next_questions: Can these frameworks be adapted to allow the system to flag its own logical constraints as revisable hypotheses rather than fixed architectural parameters?
actions.reason: Incorporating findings on SCL and SuperCorrect to address the project goal of identifying and challenging foundational assumptions.
actions.summary: Recent advances indicate that foundational reasoning axioms are best challenged through architectural separation (separating justification from cognition) and structured, teacher-guided self-correction, rather than relying on unguided self-reflection.
actions.title: Architectural and Methodological Paths to Reasoning Transparency
